main_issue: The assigned case confirms a generic attacker-controlled download URL reaching URL.openStream, but the guideline is overly framed around webhook/callback flows and its claimed four-case basis is not evidenced in this payload.
suggested_guideline: Trace attacker-controlled URL parameters and stored-but-user-supplied resource URLs into server-side URL.openStream, URLConnection, HTTP clients, download helpers, proxy clients, and redirect-following fetch routines. Review whether the exact source-to-sink path restricts allowed schemes, validates the effective destination host and resolved IP address, blocks loopback/private/link-local/metadata targets, and revalidates every redirect target before the request is made. A safe fix applies these controls before the outbound connection on the same path.
evidence_notes: case::84a39bdc311e873b9594 provides direct source-to-sink evidence: URL material is preserved as fileUrl and reaches new URL(fileUrl).openStream in CommonServiceImpl.urlDownload.
The documented repair adds only URL parsing and an http/https scheme guard; that confirms the URL-fetch mechanism but does not demonstrate host, DNS/IP-range, or redirect controls.
tempDownload is SSRF-adjacent but lower-confidence for this group because it fetches a URL obtained from stored UploadResult or OSS metadata rather than a direct request parameter.
No payload evidence describes the other three historical examples, so shared webhook/callback semantics and four-case coverage cannot be confirmed.
